title: multipart: robust streaming + tool/file payload limits + content-type validation
author: Priya Patel
description: Problem: Streaming endpoints and the OpenAI-compat layer accepted mixed content payloads inconsistently which led to silent truncation and misrouting of tool/file attachments, and unclear behavior when callers combined streaming with multipart uploads. This PR: 1) Adds a rigorous multipart/form-data validation layer for streaming and non-streaming endpoints that enforces Content-Type and boundary checks, rejects ambiguous content types, and returns clear 4xx errors with machine-readable error codes. 2) Implements per-file and per-request limits for tool/file attachments (configurable via service-level flags and per-customer overrides) with graceful backpressure for streaming uploads. 3) Fixes streaming stability issues for chunked multipart bodies by introducing a streaming parser that can handle interleaved event frames and large binary parts without buffering the whole part in memory. 4) Extends the OpenAI compatibility shim so that tool calling semantics match expected types when files are present (file->tool reference translation, and deterministic multipart ordering). 5) Adds E2E tests for Python/TS SDKs, unit tests for the parser, integration tests exercising the compatibility layer, and examples in quickstarts and docs. Migration notes: Clients that previously relied on loosely typed content-types (e.g., sending application/json with a binary body) will now receive 400 errors and should switch to multipart/form-data or application/octet-stream. Checklists: - [x] parser and validation implementation - [x] config flags and per-customer overrides - [x] OpenAI-compat mapping updates - [x] SDK tests and quickstart examples - [x] docs and release notes

release_notes: Added strict multipart/form-data validation for streaming and non-streaming endpoints. Introduced configurable per-file and per-request attachment limits and streaming parser to improve memory usage and stability. OpenAI compatibility layer: deterministic mapping of file attachments to tool references. Migration guidance: clients must use multipart/form-data for mixed JSON+file requests; ambiguous content types will be rejected; admins can temporarily disable limits via config flag.
notes_for_ops: Enable rollout: set config.disable_file_limits=true to opt out of new limits during migration; monitor metric api.multipart.rejects and infra.multipart.parser_errors. Watch for increase in 400s among older SDK versions and reach out to customers with mismatched content-types.
test_plan: Unit tests for tokenizer and validator, integration tests for chunked multipart streaming across Python/TS SDKs, load test on perf-lab focusing on large binary parts to validate memory usage, and canary rollout to 10% of hosted traffic before global flip.
